source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    To add privilege mapping use the following command:
1 ./openbmctool.py <connection options> ldap privilege-mapper create --groupName=<groupName> --privilege="priv-admin/priv-user"

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: openbmctool.py (from openbmc-tools, pip/install) + BMC + LDAP group name
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Add privilege mapping (create privilege mapping): openbmctool.py ${BMC_CONN:?operator must supply openbmctool target, e.g. http://${BMC_USER}:${BMC_PASS}@${BMC_IP}:8080/} ldap privilege-mapper create --groupName=${LDAP_GROUP:?operator must supply the LDAP group name (DN or CN)} --privilege="priv-admin/priv-user" (openbmctool from openbmc-tools, user installs + supplies the LDAP group/privilege values). Agent runs the tool and captures its output; create/delete changes BMC auth config so user confirms.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the openbmctool command output/HTTP status so the user confirms the mapping was created (200 OK).
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: changing LDAP privilege mapping affects BMC auth; use the intended group/privilege and restore if needed.

historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly requires a pinned tool, exact DN/CN and nesting semantics, dedicated non-production group/user, complete mapping baseline, one least-privilege create, mapped/control-user authorization, local recovery and cleanup.

original_test_intent: Verify openbmctool creates one exact LDAP group-to-BMC privilege mapping using the approved group identity and `priv-admin` or `priv-user` value, persists it without altering other mappings, and gives a dedicated member only the intended effective authorization.
original_method: Pin the supported openbmctool build; enumerate existing mappings and directory membership; define one unambiguous group DN/CN, selected privilege and non-production member/control accounts; preserve local recovery; create one mapping after approval; read back its stable identity; test permitted and denied non-destructive actions for the mapped user and control user; then remove only the test mapping and confirm baseline restoration.
manual_activity: An access-control owner selects the exact group identity and one least-privilege role, confirms non-production membership, permitted/denied actions and cleanup. A human retains local recovery, authorizes one create, observes real authorization and removes the test mapping. Automation may run the pinned tool and read state but cannot choose `priv-admin` by convenience or issue the verdict.
required_inputs: BMC/firmware identity, role vocabulary and pinned openbmctool/API version
Exact directory realm and group DN/CN, case and nested-membership interpretation
Selected `priv-admin` or `priv-user` role with least-privilege justification
Dedicated mapped LDAP user and unmapped/control user
Role-specific permitted and denied non-destructive action matrix
Exact cleanup/delete target and restoration procedure
safety_requirements: Do not interpret the literal `priv-admin/priv-user` as one value or arbitrarily choose administrator; approve exactly one supported role and use a dedicated non-production group.
Do not expose BMC/directory credentials in connection URLs, command lines, history, process listings, logs, screenshots or review JSON, and do not clear security/audit logs.
Resolve the group's canonical identity, realm, case, nesting and current membership before creation; stop on ambiguous or production-wide groups.
Obtain point-of-action approval for one new mapping after proving local recovery and absence of a conflicting mapping; do not bulk change, overwrite or retry.
Do not accept HTTP success or list appearance as role proof. Test effective permissions and denials with non-destructive actions from mapped and control users.

Stop on unexpected administrator access, missing expected permission, control-user privilege, local recovery failure or cleanup mismatch; remove only the identified test mapping through approved recovery.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target/tool, group identity/membership, one role, baseline, auth matrix, recovery and exact cleanup; present one create action for approval.
After approval, create one test mapping with protected authentication and capture redacted response/audit plus complete persisted readback.
Use mapped and control identities to collect non-destructive allowed/denied authorization evidence, while independently confirming local-admin access.
Remove only the approved test mapping, verify every other mapping remains unchanged, archive evidence and stop without escalation, retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve exact group DN/CN semantics, dedicated test members, one least-privilege role and effective authorization matrix.
Approve the pinned create, independent recovery and exact cleanup/delete target.
Review mapping, mapped/control authorization, audit and restoration evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its create syntax matches the source operation but does not resolve which one of `priv-admin/priv-user` is intended, whether groupName is DN or CN, or whether the mapping collides. Credential-bearing BMC_CONN and HTTP status are unsafe/inadequate, and no effective authorization or cleanup is proven.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the exact pinned openbmctool `ldap privilege-mapper create` path once with a canonical approved groupName and one supported least-privilege value, protected authentication and a known cleanup identifier.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The openbmctool create command, groupName, literal privilege choices, successful-command Criteria, no Script and 10/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review requires selection and evidence without rewriting Master.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create one uniquely identified least-privilege test mapping, prove its persisted state and actual mapped-versus-control authorization, then remove it and reconcile the entire mapping set.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected OpenBMC LDAP privilege-mapper and approved non-production directory realm.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware/API, openbmctool commit/runtime and directory server version.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Pinned openbmc-tools privilege-mapper schema, vendor BMC role model, directory group semantics and Project access-control policy.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds canonical identity, explicit role selection, effective authorization, local recovery and exact cleanup while retaining the source create command.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A vendor API override does not prove openbmctool; readback alone does not prove effective privilege; deleting the mapping alone does not prove it was correct before cleanup.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Canonical group, one role, test identities, baseline, auth matrix, recovery and cleanup.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A broad or nested group mapped to admin can escalate many users; ambiguous identifiers can create duplicate mappings; cleanup by the wrong identity can remove production access.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use a supported vendor API or WebUI only when it records the original openbmctool method, actual method, reason, engineer approval, exact mapping/auth equivalence and uncovered tool coverage. It must still exercise one real mapping and cannot replace functional authorization with read-only inspection.
expected_evidence: Approved BMC/firmware/tool version, canonical group/realm/nesting/member facts, selected role and complete redacted pre-mapping baseline
One protected create response and security audit event plus persisted mapping identity/properties without secret exposure
Mapped-user permitted and denied non-destructive actions, control/unmapped-user restrictions and independent local-admin continuity
Exact test-mapping delete/cleanup evidence and complete before/after mapping reconciliation showing no unrelated change
No retry or broad/admin production exposure and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently request creating a privilege mapping and successful command submission. The slash-separated privilege examples require a Project selection of one supported value, and group identity/effective-role details are execution-readiness inputs rather than competing purposes.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The mapping-create objective and command semantics are identifiable. The owner can supply a canonical test group, one role, safe authorization matrix and cleanup, so missing parameters make execution pending rather than permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps PACKAGE but removes credential-bearing shorthand and HTTP-only proof, resolves one role/group identity, adds effective mapped/control authorization and exact cleanup.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees with its least-privilege and recovery controls and explicitly requires full before/after mapping reconciliation tied to the next delete case.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces generic command-success evidence with persistent identity, authorization boundaries and restoration proof.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Uses the following Delete mapping only as bounded cleanup while preserving this row's independent create-and-effective-role coverage.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No invalid draft exists for this exact source identity.

review_improvement: Prevents accidental group-wide administrator escalation and false success from an HTTP response by proving exact identity, least privilege, effective authorization and cleanup.
independent_technical_reasoning: A privilege mapping is an authorization relation, not merely a stored row. Its security impact depends on canonical group resolution, nested membership and the exact role. Therefore evidence must show the intended member gains only allowed operations, the control identity does not, and local recovery remains intact; a successful create response cannot establish those properties.
